relevant_findings.finding: New masonry substrates (clay brick, CMU, cast concrete, limestone) are highly alkaline due to calcium hydroxide from Portland cement hydration. New concrete and CMU register pH 12-14. This alkalinity is the dominant factor driving primer selection — standard acrylic paints designed for surfaces pH 9 or below will suffer 'alkali burn' on uncured masonry, resulting in color loss, brittle films, and total coating failure.

Industry standard requires a 28-day cure cycle for new concrete/masonry to allow cement hydration to stabilize and surface pH to lower to 10-12 via carbonation. Accelerated coating is possible as early as 7 days using specialized high-pH primers (e.g., SW Loxon Masonry Primer) rated to withstand pH up to 13. The 7-day accelerated path requires alkali-resistant primer — this is the primary NC scenario since construction schedules rarely allow 28-day delays.

relevant_findings.topic: Block filler mandatory for CMU (PCA P12)
relevant_findings.finding: CMU has high-porosity surface with voids that must be filled before primer/topcoat application. Block filler (PCA P12 standard: Level 2 Standard Fill, minimizes voids to max 10 per SF) is MANDATORY for CMU substrate. Block filler is applied before primer as a separate task — it is a substrate preparation product, not a primer. Spray tip for block filler: 0.025-0.035 orifice (527, 531, 535). Pressure: 2,300-3,000 PSI.

Efflorescence (white powdery salt deposits from internal moisture evaporation) must be treated and removed before coating. Cleaning hierarchy: plain water + stiff brush (light) -> TSP (moderate) -> phosphoric acid (severe) -> muriatic acid 1:10-1:16 dilution (extreme, last resort). Muriatic acid requires pre-dampening masonry, scrubbing, neutralization with alkaline solution, and thorough rinsing. Moisture source must be corrected first — efflorescence indicates ongoing moisture intrusion that coating cannot solve.

relevant_findings.topic: Spray + backroll is mandatory for masonry
relevant_findings.finding: Spray on masonry = auto-add backroll. Spray bridges over pinholes/voids in porous masonry; back-rolling forces coating into pores for continuous protective film and proper DFT. This is MANDATORY per Application Methods Doctrine Part A §6. Spray-only on masonry is NOT acceptable (unlike fiber cement where backroll is avoided). Roller nap for masonry: 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch (very rough).

relevant_findings.topic: Oil-based coatings PROHIBITED on alkaline masonry
relevant_findings.finding: Oil-based and alkyd paints are strictly prohibited on alkaline masonry substrates. Alkaline hydroxides react with paint esters through saponification, hydrolyzing the binder into soft, sticky, water-soluble soap. Complete removal to bare masonry is the only remedy — no repair possible. Per Primer Systems Doctrine: alkyd is 'Not Recommended For' brick, concrete, stucco.

Two primary coating systems for masonry: (1) 100% Acrylic Latex — 10-20 perms breathability, 6-8 mils DFT, preserves texture, superior UV resistance, easier to apply/touch up. Best for structurally sound masonry. (2) Elastomeric — 5-15 perms, 20-30 mils DFT, 300-500% elongation, bridges hairline cracks. Best for cracked CMU/concrete. WARNING: elastomeric has high risk of catastrophic delamination if moisture enters from alternative sources (trapped moisture).

Maximum moisture content for masonry before coating is 12%. Moisture testing is mandatory before application. Test methods: electronic moisture meters, ASTM D4263 (Plastic Sheet Method), ASTM F1869 (Calcium Chloride Test). MC > 12% is a HARD STOP — do not coat until moisture is reduced.

Coverage rates on masonry are significantly lower than smooth substrates due to porosity and texture. Acrylic on smooth masonry: 300-350 SF/gal. Acrylic on textured/porous masonry (brick, CMU): 150-250 SF/gal. Elastomeric: even lower due to 20-30 mil DFT requirement. Block filler coverage varies by void density. Spray application adds 25-33% material waste over brush/roll baseline.

New masonry prep requires: (1) Remove waxy form-release agents and curing compounds (bond-breakers) using mechanical abrasion, abrasive blasting, or chemical detergents. (2) For CMU: apply block filler (PCA P12) to fill voids. (3) Treat efflorescence if present. (4) Verify moisture content < 12%. (5) Verify cure time (28 days standard, 7 days with Loxon-type primer).

Limestone is highly porous, acid-sensitive sedimentary stone (calcite-based). Requires breathable coatings — mineral silicate (Keim-type) at 77+ perms or high-perm acrylic (>10 perms). Standard film-forming coatings can trap moisture and cause spalling in freeze-thaw cycles. No acid cleaning on limestone — acid dissolves calcite.

relevant_findings.topic: Spalling failure mode from moisture entrapment
relevant_findings.finding: Non-breathable (impermeable) coatings trap interior vapor behind the film. Hydrostatic and osmotic pressure buildup forces paint film off wall. In freeze-thaw climates, trapped moisture freezes (water expands ~9%), shearing off the outer face of the masonry unit (spalling). Spalling exposes soft interior to rapid structural deterioration. This is the most severe masonry coating failure mode — it damages the substrate itself.

relevant_findings.topic: Spray tip and pressure for masonry coatings
relevant_findings.finding: Stucco and rough masonry tip selection: 0.017-0.021 orifice (517, 619, 621) for standard acrylic coatings. CMU block filler: 0.025-0.035 orifice (527, 531, 535). Block fillers and elastomerics require 2,300-3,000 PSI. Standard exterior latex: 1,500-2,500 PSI. Filter mesh: 60-mesh (black/medium) for latex paints, 30-mesh (gray/coarse) for block fillers and elastomerics.

relevant_findings.topic: Substrate pre-wetting in high heat conditions
relevant_findings.finding: In high-heat/low-humidity conditions, porous masonry wicks water from paint film causing flash drying and poor adhesion. Lightly misting the masonry surface with water before application prevents substrate from stealing moisture from the coating. This is an SOP-level procedure note, not an estimation factor.

condition_drivers.impact: Drives block filler requirement (CMU only), coating breathability selection (limestone requires high-perm), surface texture (affects production rates and material coverage), and cleaning method restrictions (no acid on limestone).
condition_drivers.notes: This is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION. Brick is dense, relatively smooth. CMU is porous with voids requiring block filler. Concrete is variable. Limestone requires special breathable coatings.

condition_drivers.impact: Drives full prep sequence: cure verification, moisture testing, efflorescence treatment, form-release removal, block filler (CMU), alkali-resistant primer. This is the only NC-relevant state.
condition_drivers.notes: SS_EXT_BARE_MASONRY is the single NC state for this spec. All new masonry arrives bare — there is no factory-primed masonry equivalent. Repaint states (sound, failing, efflorescence-recurrence) would require a separate repaint spec.

condition_drivers.impact: Acrylic: standard coating for structurally sound masonry (6-8 mils DFT, 10-20 perms, 300-350 SF/gal smooth, 150-250 SF/gal textured). Elastomeric: crack-bridging coating for cracked/deficient masonry (20-30 mils DFT, 300-500% elongation, significantly lower coverage). Elastomeric requires moisture entrapment risk assessment.
condition_drivers.notes: This is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION. Mineral silicate (Keim) is excluded from QT scope — it is a specialty historic preservation system outside standard residential painting.

condition_drivers.impact: QT2: economy — light clean, single finish coat on primed surface, economy 100% acrylic. QT3: standard — full clean, dedicated primer, two finish coats, mid-grade acrylic. QT4: premium — TSP wash, premium primer, two finish coats with premium materials, raking light inspection between coats.
condition_drivers.notes: QT5 not applicable to masonry wall field — reserved for fine exterior millwork only. QT2 may accept single finish coat on properly primed masonry per substrate condition.

condition_drivers.impact: Spray_backroll is the gold standard for masonry (400-600 SF/hr). Roll is the fallback for smaller areas or occupied-adjacent (150-400 SF/hr). Brush is for detail work and small areas only (50-100 SF/hr). IMPORTANT: spray on masonry ALWAYS requires backroll — there is no spray-only option.
condition_drivers.notes: This is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION. spray_backroll requires 2-person crew. Roll provides excellent mechanical bond with minimal masking. Brush is never the primary method for masonry wall field.

condition_drivers.impact: Height modifier on all tasks at elevation. ground=1.00, ladder=1.35, scaffold=1.60, lift=1.50. Applied per elevation based on working height. Scaffold is particularly common for masonry (heavy staging for long-duration work at height).
condition_drivers.notes: Treated as a HEIGHT MODIFIER (like FAC_HEIGHT for interior), not a site condition. A project may have ground access on one elevation and scaffold on another.

quality_differences.description: Economy exterior masonry. Light water wash. Alkali-resistant primer (still mandatory on new masonry — pH hazard is not quality-optional). Single finish coat acceptable on properly primed surface. Economy-grade 100% acrylic exterior. No edge precision required.
quality_differences.typical_use: Commercial/industrial masonry, rental property, budget-constrained. Block filler on CMU is still mandatory at QT2.

quality_differences.description: Standard residential masonry. Full water wash with stiff brush. Efflorescence treatment if present. Alkali-resistant primer. Two finish coats with mid-grade 100% acrylic. Clean transitions at trim/window interfaces. Block filler on CMU. Caulk masonry-to-trim joints.
quality_differences.typical_use: Standard homeowner NC masonry, most residential exterior masonry painting.

quality_differences.description: Premium exterior masonry. Full TSP wash. Efflorescence treatment. Premium alkali-resistant primer. Two finish coats with premium materials (SW Duration, BM Aura). Raking light inspection before second coat. Crisp trim lines. Block filler on CMU with verification pass.
quality_differences.typical_use: High-end residential, showcase homes, architectural masonry where coating quality is paramount.

failure_modes.name: Alkali burn / saponification
failure_modes.description: Standard acrylic paints applied to uncured alkaline masonry (pH 12-14) suffer chemical destruction of the binder. Alkali hydroxides attack pigments and binders, causing color loss, brittle films, and total coating failure. Oil-based coatings are even more vulnerable — alkaline hydroxides hydrolyze esters into soft, sticky soap (saponification).
failure_modes.prevention: Use alkali-resistant primer rated to pH 13 (e.g., SW Loxon Masonry Primer) on all new masonry. NEVER use oil-based or alkyd products on alkaline masonry. Verify cure age (28-day standard, 7-day minimum with Loxon-type primer).
failure_modes.detection: Soft, sticky paint film. Color loss or yellowing. Paint easily scrapes off. Film dissolution on oil-based products.

failure_modes.name: Moisture entrapment and delamination
failure_modes.description: Non-breathable (impermeable) coatings trap interior vapor behind film. Hydrostatic and osmotic pressure buildup forces paint film off the wall. Particularly severe with elastomeric coatings (5-15 perms) if moisture enters from alternate sources (rain intrusion, rising damp, interior humidity).
failure_modes.prevention: Verify MC < 12% before coating. Use breathable coatings (acrylic at 10-20 perms preferred). Assess moisture sources before specifying elastomeric. Ensure proper wall drainage and flashing.
failure_modes.detection: Blistering or bubbling of paint film. Delamination in sheets. Damp spots behind coating. Efflorescence pushing through film.

failure_modes.name: Spalling from freeze-thaw
failure_modes.description: Trapped moisture behind impermeable coating freezes in cold weather — water expands approximately 9%. Internal pressure shears off the outer face of the masonry unit, exposing soft interior to rapid structural deterioration. This failure mode damages the substrate itself, not just the coating.
failure_modes.prevention: Use breathable coatings. Verify moisture source control. Avoid elastomeric coatings in freeze-thaw climates unless moisture source is fully controlled. High-perm acrylic (>10 perms) preferred in freeze-thaw regions.
failure_modes.detection: Face of brick or block fracturing. Loose masonry fragments at base of wall. Exposed raw masonry interior. Hollow sound when tapped.

failure_modes.name: Efflorescence recurrence
failure_modes.description: Salt deposits push paint film off surface from behind. Indicates ongoing moisture intrusion that coating alone cannot solve. Efflorescence returns even after cleaning if the moisture source is not corrected.
failure_modes.prevention: Identify and correct moisture source before coating. Remove all existing efflorescence. Do not coat over active efflorescence. Note: efflorescence treatment is a prep task — it does not prevent recurrence if the moisture source remains.
failure_modes.detection: White crystalline deposits on or under paint film. Paint blistering with white powder underneath. Recurring salt deposits after cleaning.

failure_modes.name: Coating applied to uncured masonry (< 7 days)
failure_modes.description: Masonry coated before minimum 7-day cure (with alkali-resistant primer) or 28-day cure (with standard primer) will have actively hydrating cement that releases calcium hydroxide, elevating pH beyond tolerable range for any architectural coating.
failure_modes.prevention: Verify cure age before coating. 28-day minimum for standard primer systems. 7-day minimum with alkali-resistant primer (Loxon-type) rated to pH 13. Document cure date on project record.
failure_modes.detection: Widespread coating failure within weeks of application. Blistering, peeling, discoloration across entire surface (not localized).

failure_modes.name: Holidays from insufficient backroll
failure_modes.description: Spray application without proper backroll leaves pinholes and voids in porous masonry surface uncovered. These 'holidays' (thin spots) allow moisture penetration and accelerate localized coating failure.
failure_modes.prevention: Mandatory backroll on all spray-applied masonry coatings. Second technician follows sprayer immediately with 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch nap roller. Backroll while coating is still wet.
failure_modes.detection: Pinhole-sized bare spots visible on close inspection. Premature localized peeling or staining at void locations.

notes_for_materials_manager: ALL new masonry requires alkali-resistant primer (e.g., SW Loxon Masonry Primer or equivalent) — standard acrylic primer is NOT suitable for pH 12-14 surfaces. This is non-negotiable regardless of quality tier.

CMU substrate auto-adds block filler (PCA P12 standard). Block filler is a separate material from primer — it fills voids, not seals surface. Heavy-body product requiring 0.025-0.035 orifice spray tips and 30-mesh (gray/coarse) filters.

Two coating system branches: acrylic (300-350 SF/gal smooth, 150-250 SF/gal textured) and elastomeric (significantly lower coverage due to 20-30 mil DFT). Elastomeric requires moisture entrapment risk flag.
Spray application adds 25-33% material waste over brush/roll baseline. Factor into material quantities for spray_backroll method.
Roller nap for masonry: 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch (very rough substrate). Nylon/polyester blend for water-based products.
Spray tip for masonry topcoat: 517, 619, 621 (0.017-0.021 orifice). 60-mesh (black) filter for latex. Replace tip at 15-40 gallon interval.
Efflorescence cleaning materials: TSP, phosphoric acid, muriatic acid (1:10-1:16 dilution). Stiff bristle brushes. Neutralizing agent (ammonia or baking soda).
Caulk for masonry-to-trim joints: polyurethane (Class 25/50) or hybrid MS polymer — requires 3-7 day cure before painting if polyurethane. Siliconized acrylic acceptable for low-movement joints.
Oil-based and alkyd products are PROHIBITED on masonry — include as a material blocker rule.
Masking tape for masonry: Red stucco poly tape (7.0 mil, 30-day UV rating) for rough masonry/stucco surfaces. Standard blue tape will not adhere to textured masonry.
notes_for_sop_librarian: Module structure: setup -> protect -> clean -> prep -> block_fill (CMU only) -> prime -> apply -> cleanup -> teardown.
Cure verification task is FIRST in prep sequence — must verify 28-day cure (standard) or 7-day cure (with Loxon-type primer) before any coating work. Document cure date.
Moisture testing task (MC < 12%) is mandatory before primer application. HARD STOP if MC > 12%.
Efflorescence treatment is a conditional prep task — only when efflorescence is present. Cleaning method escalates by severity (water -> TSP -> phosphoric acid -> muriatic acid).
Form-release agent removal is a prep task for cast concrete — mechanical abrasion or chemical detergent. Not applicable to brick or CMU.
Block filler (CMU only) is a SEPARATE MODULE between prep and prime. It is not a primer — it fills voids. Applied by spray (heavy tip) or heavy roller.
Spray on masonry = ALWAYS add backroll task. No spray-only option. Second technician follows sprayer with 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch nap roller while coating is wet.
Oil-based products are BLOCKED in material selection for this spec. Hard stop if oil-based is selected.
Substrate pre-wetting (light mist with water) before application in high-heat/low-humidity conditions — SOP procedure note, not a separate task.
Caulking at masonry-to-trim joints is a prep module task. Polyurethane caulk requires 3-7 day cure before painting.
Light sand between coats at QT4 only (not QT2 or QT3).
Elastomeric coating system requires moisture source assessment as a pre-coating decision gate — document in project record.
notes_for_estimation_engineer: Production rates by method: spray_backroll 400-600 SF/hr (gold standard), roll 150-400 SF/hr, brush 50-100 SF/hr (detail only).
Block filler application rate: spray 200-350 SF/hr (heavy material, large tip, high pressure).
Access modifier (FAC_EXT_ACCESS): ground=1.00, ladder=1.35, scaffold=1.60, lift=1.50. Scaffold is common for masonry due to heavy staging needs.
Material coverage: acrylic on smooth masonry 300-350 SF/gal, acrylic on textured/porous 150-250 SF/gal, elastomeric significantly lower.
Efflorescence treatment rate: ~100-200 SF/hr depending on severity and method (water wash faster, acid wash slower).
Cure verification and moisture testing: fixed time per project (~0.5-1 hr), not area-scaled.
Form-release removal (cast concrete only): ~100-150 SF/hr mechanical abrasion.
Masking-to-spray ratio: 3:1 to 4:1 (masking hours to spray hours). Masking is a separate line item.
Environmental conditions (wind, dew point, sun, temp) are EXCLUDED from estimation — they are SOP/process concerns, not estimatable at bid time.
Coat system: 1 alkali-resistant primer + 2 finish coats standard at QT3/QT4. QT2 may use single finish coat on properly primed surface.
CMU projects add block filler as a separate line item (material + labor) before primer.
Caulk masonry-to-trim joints: 75-150 LF/hr depending on joint complexity.
Scaffold setup/teardown for masonry: 1.75-2.5 hrs setup per facade, 1.0-1.5 hrs teardown per facade (2-person crew). Must be a distinct line item.

assumptions.value: New construction masonry wall coating — brick, CMU, cast concrete, limestone. Exterior wall field surfaces only.
assumptions.note: Trim around masonry openings is covered by separate exterior trim spec. Foundation coatings below grade are excluded.

assumptions.value: Mandatory on all spray-applied masonry coatings. No spray-only option.
assumptions.note: Explicit doctrine guidance: 'Stucco and porous masonry: Spray bridges over pinholes/voids; back-rolling forces coating into pores for continuous protective film.'

assumptions.value: Mineral silicate (Keim-type) coatings excluded from this spec — specialty historic preservation system
assumptions.note: Mineral silicate at 77+ perms is the ultimate breathable masonry coating but requires specialized application (chemically bonds via silicification). Not standard residential painting scope. Could be a separate spec if needed.

assumptions.value: QT5 not applicable to masonry wall field applications
assumptions.source: Sibling spec pattern (fiber cement, wood siding)
assumptions.note: QT5 reserved for fine exterior millwork, columns, decorative elements. Not wall field surfaces.

assumptions.value: This spec covers new construction only. Single substrate state (SS_EXT_BARE_MASONRY).
assumptions.note: Repaint masonry (sound, failing, efflorescence-recurrence) would require a separate spec with fundamentally different prep modules and substrate state branching.

uncertainties.detail: Block filler coverage varies dramatically by CMU void density — lightweight block has more voids than standard weight. Doctrine states 'coverage varies by void density' but does not provide specific rates. Industry range is approximately 75-125 SF/gal for standard CMU.
uncertainties.recommendation: Use 100 SF/gal as baseline for block filler material estimation. Flag for field calibration.

uncertainties.detail: Elastomeric coatings at 20-30 mils DFT require significantly more material per pass than standard acrylic. Production rates for elastomeric spray_backroll are not explicitly provided in doctrine. Likely slower than acrylic due to heavier material.
uncertainties.recommendation: Estimate elastomeric spray_backroll at 60-75% of acrylic rate (approximately 250-400 SF/hr). Flag for field calibration.

uncertainties.detail: Doctrine identifies limestone as requiring breathable coatings and prohibiting acid cleaning, but does not provide specific product recommendations for residential limestone coating beyond 'mineral silicate or high-perm acrylic (>10 perms)'. Most residential limestone scenarios will use high-perm acrylic.
uncertainties.recommendation: Default limestone to high-perm acrylic system. Note acid cleaning prohibition in SOP. Add limestone as a substrate_type variant.

uncertainties.detail: Doctrine identifies form-release agents as bond-breakers requiring removal by mechanical abrasion, abrasive blasting, or chemical detergents, but does not provide production rates for this prep task.
uncertainties.recommendation: Estimate mechanical abrasion for form-release removal at 100-150 SF/hr. Flag for field calibration.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray_backroll
zones.notes: LF-based — measured along house perimeter where landscape is adjacent. Roll: drop cloth at base. Spray_backroll: full tarp width over plantings.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray_backroll
zones.notes: Adjacent walkways. Roll: drop cloth runners. Spray_backroll: full tarp coverage.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray_backroll
zones.notes: Adjacent patio surfaces. Protection level driven by proximity and application method.
Exterior light fixtures mounted on or adjacent to masonry wall. Bag or tape over fixture.
HVAC condenser units adjacent to masonry wall. Full tarp cover during spray operations. Shutdown protocol per Protection Doctrine.

protection_zones_analysis.cross_spec_protection_note: Window and door protection during masonry wall work is NOT this spec's responsibility. Window/door masking belongs in the respective window or door spec. This prevents double-counting and ensures protection responsibility is clear per surface owner.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Window casing or masonry opening trim. Masonry terminates at opening. No cut-in — trim is a separate spec.
Door casing trim. Same as window casing relationship. Separate spec.
Soffit underside at eave/parapet junction. Often different color. Separate scope.
Foundation below masonry wall. Not painted in this scope. Drop cloth protection at grade level.
Frieze or band board at masonry-to-soffit junction (if present). Separate trim scope.

adjacency_analysis.key_finding: Masonry wall field has NO edge work requirements within this spec. All adjacent surfaces are separate specs (trim, soffit, foundation) or not in scope. Protection relationships only. Masonry terminates at openings and trim elements. Window/door protection owned by window/door specs.

affected_conditions.notes: Access type drives a HEIGHT MODIFIER on tasks. Applied per elevation based on working height. Scaffold is particularly common for masonry (heavy, long-duration work). Sectional scaffold preferred for masonry over pump jacks.

excluded_conditions.rationale: Environmental conditions are important to the painting PROCESS but are NOT estimatable. They are unpredictable, change daily, and cannot be set as fixed conditions for an estimate. They belong in SOP procedure notes and job-site decision protocols, not in production rate modifiers.

excluded.reason: Unpredictable. Changes hourly. Cannot set a fixed modifier for estimate.
Varies by time of day, sun angle, and season. Not predictable at bid time.
Weather-dependent. Not predictable at bid time.
Varies by elevation and season. Scheduling concern, not estimation.

valid_input_states.rationale: NC masonry arrives bare — there is no factory-primed masonry equivalent. All new masonry is bare, alkaline, and requires full prime system. Single substrate state simplifies this NC spec.

output_state.rationale: Output state is the painted finish. Satin is the most common exterior masonry sheen (hides surface irregularities while providing durability). Actual output varies by sheen configuration (flat, satin).

adjacent_state_protection_analysis.rationale: Protect finished trim from masonry spray overspray. Unfinished trim needs no protection — it will be painted later.
Soffit is typically painted before walls (top-down sequencing). If already finished, light masking at the wall-soffit junction.
Foundation wall is rarely painted in NC context. Drop cloth at grade level handled by landscape/hardscape protection zones.

exterior_substrate_states.description: New, uncoated masonry surface (brick, CMU, cast concrete, or limestone). Highly alkaline (pH 12-14 for new concrete/CMU). Requires full primer system with alkali-resistant primer.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Verify cure age (28 days standard, 7 days minimum with Loxon-type primer). Moisture test (MC < 12% mandatory). Remove form-release agents/curing compounds on cast concrete. Treat efflorescence if present. Apply block filler on CMU (PCA P12).
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: Alkali-resistant primer rated to pH 13 (e.g., SW Loxon Masonry Primer). Standard acrylic primer NOT suitable for new alkaline masonry.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: This is the only NC state for masonry. All new masonry is bare and alkaline. The 7-day accelerated path with Loxon-type primer is the most common NC scenario since construction schedules rarely allow 28-day delays.

exterior_access_type_analysis.treatment: Modifier on tasks, not a site condition. Same concept as FAC_HEIGHT for interior.

scenarios.notes: Single-story masonry, first 8 ft. No ladder needed. Baseline rate.
Two-story masonry, areas above 8 ft. Constant repositioning. Safety overhead.
Preferred for masonry at height — heavy staging, long-duration work. Better ergonomics than ladder for masonry backroll operations. Setup/teardown is a separate line item.
Boom/scissor lift for 3+ story or difficult access. Requires firm ground. Rental cost.

exterior_environmental_constraints.note: Environmental constraints are documented here for SOP reference but are EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers per established exterior spec convention.

sop_reference_only.go_range: 50-90 degrees F surface temperature for masonry
sop_reference_only.note: Below 50: slow cure, adhesion risk. Above 90: improper cure, alkali burn risk, bubbling.

sop_reference_only.rule: Surface temp must be >= 5 degrees F above dew point
sop_reference_only.note: Adhesion and blushing risk at marginal conditions.
Test with electronic moisture meter, ASTM D4263 plastic sheet, or ASTM F1869 calcium chloride.

sop_reference_only.rule: 28 days standard, 7 days minimum with alkali-resistant primer
sop_reference_only.note: New concrete/CMU pH 12-14. Must verify cure age before any coating work.

sop_reference_only.rule: Lightly mist porous masonry in high-heat/low-humidity conditions before application
sop_reference_only.note: Prevents substrate from wicking water from paint film.

spray_backroll_acrylic.notes: Gold standard for masonry. Airless spray with immediate backroll. 2-person crew. 517/619/621 tip. Higher end for long uninterrupted runs on smooth brick.

spray_backroll_elastomeric.notes: Heavier material, higher DFT (20-30 mils). Slower than acrylic. Heavy-duty tip (0.021-0.025) required. 2,300-3,000 PSI.

roll_acrylic.notes: Roller only. 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch nap. Excellent mechanical bond. Higher end on smooth brick, lower on heavily textured CMU.

roll_elastomeric.notes: Heavier material, multiple passes for DFT build. Slower than acrylic roller application.

brush.notes: Detail work, small areas, trim interfaces only. Not a primary method for masonry wall field.

block_filler_spray.notes: CMU only. Heavy-body material. 527/531/535 tip. 30-mesh filter. 2,300-3,000 PSI.

block_filler_roll.notes: CMU only. Heavy roller application. 1-1/2 inch nap.

alkali_resistant_primer_spray_backroll.notes: Primer on bare masonry. Spray + backroll (mandatory). Similar to topcoat rate — primer is thinner bodied.

efflorescence_treatment_light.notes: Water + stiff brush. Light salt deposits.

efflorescence_treatment_acid.notes: Acid wash + neutralization. Severe deposits. Includes pre-dampening, scrubbing, neutralizing, rinsing.

form_release_removal.notes: Cast concrete only. Mechanical abrasion or chemical detergent.

moisture_testing.notes: Fixed time per project. Electronic meter readings at multiple locations.

caulk_masonry_joints.notes: Masonry-to-trim joint caulking. Gun + finger tool. Backer rod adds time.

water_wash.notes: Low-pressure water wash for new masonry. Stiff brush for stubborn areas.

key_decisions.decision: Combined (full phase_scope). Prime and finish phases have unique task keys within the single spec.
key_decisions.rationale: NC masonry painting is a single-mobilization scope — same crew primes and paints. Each phase (block_fill, prime, finish) has its own task IDs and module IDs for independent rate tracking and phase-level reporting. Matches siding sibling spec pattern.

key_decisions.decision: Include substrate_type dimension: brick, CMU, concrete, limestone.
key_decisions.rationale: Substrate type drives block filler requirement (CMU only), cleaning restrictions (no acid on limestone), breathability requirements (limestone needs high-perm), and surface texture affecting production rates.

Coating system drives DFT requirements (6-8 mils vs 20-30 mils), material consumption (dramatically different coverage rates), production rates, and moisture risk assessment. Mineral silicate excluded as specialty historic system.

key_decisions.decision: Block filler is a SEPARATE MODULE triggered only by substrate_type = CMU.
key_decisions.rationale: Block filler is not a primer — it fills voids in porous CMU to create a smooth, paintable surface (PCA P12). It has its own material, application method, and production rate distinct from primer and topcoat. Brick, concrete, and limestone do not require block filler.

key_decisions.decision: Application method 'spray_backroll' is a single unit — there is no spray-only option for masonry.
key_decisions.rationale: Per Exterior Application Methods Doctrine: spray on porous masonry mandates back-rolling to force coating into pores. Unlike fiber cement where backroll is avoided, masonry REQUIRES it. The 'spray_backroll' method is treated as a single production rate, not two separate tasks.

key_decisions.decision: Oil-based and alkyd products are PROHIBITED for this spec. Hard blocker rule.
key_decisions.rationale: Saponification on alkaline masonry is catastrophic and irreversible. Oil-based primers and coatings must be blocked at the material selection stage. No exceptions.

All new masonry arrives bare — there is no factory-primed masonry. Repaint states (sound existing, failed existing, efflorescence-recurrence) require fundamentally different prep modules and would be a separate spec.

key_decisions.decision: NOT this spec's responsibility. Per established exterior spec convention.
key_decisions.rationale: Window/door protection belongs in window/door specs. Prevents double-counting. Clear ownership per surface.

key_decisions.decision: EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers. Per established exterior spec convention.
key_decisions.rationale: Environmental conditions are unpredictable at bid time. They are SOP/process concerns documented for field reference but not included in production rate modifiers.

key_decisions.decision: 1 alkali-resistant primer + 2 finish coats standard at QT3/QT4. Block filler (CMU only) precedes primer. QT2 may accept single finish coat.
key_decisions.rationale: Masonry requires dedicated alkali-resistant primer (non-negotiable on new alkaline surfaces). Two topcoats provide proper DFT and film build for durability. Block filler on CMU is a separate pre-primer step.

key_decisions.decision: Cure verification and moisture testing are FIXED-TIME tasks (per project), not area-scaled.
key_decisions.rationale: Checking cure age and moisture content takes the same time regardless of wall area — it is a set of spot readings and documentation, not a per-SF operation.

key_decisions.decision: Elastomeric coating selection triggers a mandatory moisture source assessment note in project documentation.
key_decisions.rationale: Elastomeric coatings (5-15 perms) have high risk of catastrophic delamination if moisture enters from alternate sources. The coating system choice requires documentation of moisture source control assessment.

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Drives block filler requirement, cleaning method restrictions, and breathability requirements. Not captured by existing PS keys.
proposed_new_keys.notes: Per-elevation or per-wall section if mixed masonry types on same structure.

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Drives DFT, material consumption, production rate, and moisture risk assessment. Project-level configuration.
proposed_new_keys.notes: Elastomeric selection triggers moisture source assessment documentation requirement.
